t: This is The World Turned Upside Down, a big sculpture on Sheffield Street, on the campus of the London School of Economics. It's a globe, about thirteen feet across, balanced on its North Pole. It was unveiled in March 2019, and was reportedly paid for by alumni donations, at a cost of over two hundred thousand pounds. The name comes from a seventeenth-century English ballad. It's by Mark Wallinger, who won the Turner Prize in 2007 and made Ecce Homo, the first work to stand on Trafalgar Square's empty fourth plinth.
